sentences.text:
Baljinder Singh Alias Sonu vs State Of Punjab And Another on 4
February, 2026

Author: Jasjit Singh Bedi
Bench: Jasjit Singh Bedi

264
 In The High Court Of Punjab And Haryana At

Chandigarh
 Crm-M-53702-2025
 Date of decision :04.02.2026
 Baljinder Singh Alias Sonu
 ... Petitioner
 Versus
State Of Punjab And Another
 ...Respondents

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Jasjit Singh Bedi
Present: Mr. Inderpal Singh, Advocate
 for the petitioner.
Mr. M.S. Toor, A.A.G., Punjab.

Ms. Arshdeep Kaur, Advocate
 for respondent No.2.
 (Through Video Conferencing)
 ****
Jasjit Singh Bedi, J. (Oral)

The prayer in this petition is for quashing of an FIR No.199 dated 21.08.2019 (Annexure P-1)
registered under Sections 419, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471 IPC and Section 12 of Passports Act, 1967 at Police Station Beas, District Amritsar, Punjab along with all consequential proceedings arising therefrom on the basis of a compromise arrived at between the parties.

Vide order dated 23.09.2025 this Court had directed the parties to appear before Illaqa Magistrate for getting their statements recorded with regard to the compromise dated 29.08.2025 (P-2).
The
Illaqa Magistrate/trial Court was to submit a report in this regard giving certain details as enumerated in the said order.

sentences.text: Pursuant to the order dated 23.09.2025 passed by this Court, the parties have appeared before the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Baba Bakala Sahib, District Amritsar and as per the report dated 06.01.2026 submitted to this Court, both the parties have got recorded their respective statements in Court.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Baba Bakala Sahib
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: A perusal of the aforesaid report would show that the parties have effected a genuine compromise without there being any pressure, coercion or undue influence.
In view of the compromise there is a remote possibility of the complainant coming forward to support the prosecution case.

The powers under Section 482 Cr.PC can be exercised in such like situation in order to prevent unnecessary vagaries of criminal trial to be faced by the parties, when there are remote chances of conviction of the accused.

The compromise in question is found to be fully in consonance with the direction issued by the Court in "Kulwinder Singh & Ors. Vs. State of Punjab 2007(3) RCR (Criminal) 1052 and Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr., 2012(4) RCR (Crl.) 543".

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the aforesaid report of the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Baba Bakala Sahib,
District Amritsar accompanied by statements of both the parties, the FIR No.199 dated 21.08.2019 (Annexure P-1) registered under Sections 419, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471 IPC and Section 12 of Passports Act, 1967 at Police Station Beas, District Amritsar, Punjab along with all consequential proceedings arising therefrom are hereby quashed qua the petitioner.
Petition stands disposed of.
(JASJIT SINGH BEDI)

Pursuant to the order dated 23.09.2025 passed by this Court, the parties have appeared before the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Baba Bakala Sahib, District Amritsar and as per the report dated 06.01.2026 submitted to this Court, both the parties have got recorded their respective statements in Court.
A perusal of the aforesaid report would show that the parties have effected a genuine compromise without there being any pressure, coercion or undue influence.
In view of the compromise there is a remote possibility of the complainant coming forward to support the prosecution case.
The powers under Section 482 Cr.PC can be exercised in such like situation in order to prevent unnecessary vagaries of criminal trial to be faced by the parties, when there are remote chances of conviction of the accused.
